title: One hundred selected worm response triples exceed a steady passive bound that can fail at finite time
abstract: We tested a steady passive transfer bound in pooled C. elegans calcium responses. Measured self-responses remove unknown positive source and target gains from a path-product ratio. Of 1171 selected WT ordered triples, 100 exceeded one. The largest ratio was 6.680741, which needs at least a factor 1.607704 on each of four means to remove that single constraint. No reciprocal self-response bound failed in 82 selected pairs. Stricter occurrence and detection rules retained triple failures. Only 3 of 54 triples selected by electrical contacts failed, with maximum correction factor 1.074407. These are deterministic constraints on a steady proxy, not physiological rejections. A passive three-cell chain has a finite-window mean ratio that tends to 4/3, so finite measurement windows alone can violate the bound. Pooled animals, calcium readout, shared entries and unknown amplitude error limit inference. Original code, proofs, aggregate results, static figures, source hashes and external retrieval steps support reproduction.
